Wide painted seascape at night, camera low on the water. Two dark rounded headlands curve toward each other, leaving a narrow, sheltered cove of still black water between them, a sandy beach at its far end with one warm lamp glowing in a tent. A tall ship under a single great red sail glides slowly into the cove, its prow parting the glassy water in a long V-shaped wake, the sail full and curved, lamplight from the shore catching its edge. Thousands of tiny floating river-lamps drift out of the cove around the hull. Purple-violet #d98fa8 night sky with a low moon, warm amber #e0a33c lamplight on the water. Slow, heavy, inevitable, sensual. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
